summary:
Radar for 2026-11-27, the day after Thanksgiving. The holiday-table window closes today. There are two fresh hooks. (1) The 2nd mainstream wave on the GLP-1 NAION eye warning. Health Canada's semaglutide warning ran 25–26 Nov on CBC, CTV, Globe and Mail, Toronto Star and Global News. The FDA's class-wide label change from 9 Nov covers tirzepatide and Foundayo, with a meta-analysis of 126 trials: 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 person-years. (2) Sleep apnea results from randomized trials of two drugs people search by name. Foundayo's ATTAIN-OSA showed about 17–18 fewer breathing events per hour at 52 weeks, and Lilly plans to file with the FDA by the end of 2026. Retatrutide's TRIUMPH-OSA showed −34.3 vs −9.9 events per hour at 80 weeks. The best fast-turn long video is Foundayo sleep apnea: a searched approved drug name, a fresh RCT and thin creator coverage. It must be framed as a trial result, not an approved use, and linked to the Foundayo What to Expect video. The NAION topic is best served by the Serious Risks video already in the queue plus a Canada-hooked Short. Don't make a duplicate long video. The required search-demand formats stay in the list (6-month timeline, hair loss, nausea, pen injection sites, pill vs injection head-to-head). New felt-symptom Short ideas: semaglutide skin sensitivity (dysesthesia is now on the label) and next-morning GI symptoms. Observational stories (breast density, sperm, cancer umbrella review) are caution or chapter-only. Compounded price lists, 'GLP-1 chocolate', gray-market retatrutide busts, animal-only data and the BrightGene China pipeline are rejected.

Sources: [Finviz/Lilly ATTAIN-OSA](https://finviz.com/news/419221/lillys-foundayo-orforglipron-significantly-reduced-obstructive-sleep-apnea-severity-reinforcing-its-potential-to-improve-health-beyond-weight-loss), [TCTMD](https://www.tctmd.com/news/attain-osa-oral-glp-1-linked-fewer-breathing-interruptions), [Fierce Pharma](https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/lilly-heads-fda-phase-3-foundayo-win-sleep-apnea), [Healio TRIUMPH-OSA](https://www.healio.com/news/pulmonology/20261111/triumphosa-retatrutide-reduces-sleep-apnea-severity-in-osa-plus-obesity), [Pharmacy Times NAION](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/fda-requires-class-wide-glp-1-ra-labeling-changes-for-potential-naion-risk), [Benefits and Pensions Monitor](https://www.benefitsandpensionsmonitor.com/news/industry-news/us-fda-adds-the-glp-1-eye-risk-warning-canada-already-requires/394418), [Pharmacy Times dysesthesia](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/semaglutide-associated-sensory-skin-disturbance-in-patients-without-diabetes-treated-for-weight-loss), [Pharmaceutical Journal](https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/dysaesthesia-added-to-semaglutide-side-effects-list).

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) and sleep apnea: what the ATTAIN-OSA randomized trial showed at 52 weeks
candidates.angle: Fast-turn long video (Exp I), titled on the result: 'Foundayo (Orforglipron) for Sleep Apnea: What Did the Trial Show?' Sentence 1 gives the answer: about 17–18 fewer breathing interruptions an hour vs placebo, with 10–11% weight loss vs 1–2%. Second payoff: about 3 in 10 people not using CPAP reached remission or mild OSA. State plainly that it is not yet approved for sleep apnea (Lilly plans to file by the end of 2026). Zepbound is the drug already approved for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Link from the old Foundayo video (LWyUfli67CI); watch-next target is Foundayo What to Expect (ssb7Zcs3KSY). No dosing.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks (FDA submission news by year end refreshes it)
candidates.why_now: A phase 3 RCT result for a drug people search by name ('foundayo', 'orforglipron' already bring our old video about 60 min a day). Trade and medical press (HCPLive 24 Nov, TCTMD, Fierce, Healio) have covered it, but health creators have barely touched it. This is the EloraTZP pattern.

evidence.signal: Met primary AHI endpoint at 52 weeks; hypoxic burden down up to 55.9%; FDA submission planned by end of 2026
About 17–18 fewer breathing events an hour vs placebo; 10–11% weight loss vs 1–2%
'Orforglipron Reduces Sleep Apnea Severity in ATTAIN-OSA'
Lilly seeks to expand the Foundayo label after the phase 3 OSA win

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) and the GLP-1 eye warning (NAION): how rare it is, now that Health Canada has flagged semaglutide
candidates.angle: Don't make a new long video. Serious Risks (re-timed, in the queue) already covers NAION, so fold this news hook into its description and pinned comment. Make one calm Short for Canada, US, UK and AU viewers, tirzepatide first: 'Mounjaro now carries the same rare eye warning as Ozempic. Here's how rare.' Give one rounded number: about 6 vs 4 cases per 100,000 person-years in the FDA's pooled trials. Include the same-day action: sudden, painless vision loss in one eye means urgent care. Never say stop the medicine; say talk to your prescriber. Short target: Serious Risks, or Side Effects until it's live.
candidates.why_now: A second mainstream wave on 25–26 Nov (CBC, CTV, Globe and Mail, Toronto Star, Global News 'How rare is the very rare risk'). The FDA's 9 Nov class-wide label change explicitly includes tirzepatide and Foundayo. Our NAION TikTok reached 648.

evidence.signal: FDA class-wide NAION labeling incl. tirzepatide and orforglipron; 126-RCT meta-analysis 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years
Canada's Wegovy monograph listed NAION as very rare (Sept 2026), before the FDA
'How rare is the very rare risk of vision loss from GLP-1 drugs?' 26 Nov

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and sleep apnea: TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA phase 3 randomized trials (80 weeks)
candidates.angle: Pipeline result explained as a trial result, never as available or 'better than Zepbound'. AHI fell 34.3 vs 9.9 events per hour on 9 mg in adults without diabetes; the 4 mg dose missed significance. Best as a chapter in the Foundayo sleep apnea video ('the next wave'), or a long video only if it's fast-turned with a strong anti-gray-market line. It's not approved anywhere, so never point to a source.
